title: Extinction
author: Wikipedia contributors
attribution: Wikipedia contributors, “Extinction”, English Wikipedia. Text available under CC BY-SA 4.0; see source history for contributors.
paragraphs: Extinction is the termination of a species via the death of its last member. A taxon may become functionally extinct before the death of its last member if it loses the capacity to reproduce and recover. As a species' potential range may be very large, determining this moment is difficult, and is usually done retrospectively. This difficulty leads to phenomena such as Lazarus taxa, where a species presumed extinct abruptly "reappears" (typically in the fossil record) after a period of apparent absence.

Over five billion species are estimated to have died out. It is estimated that there are currently around 8.7 million species of eukaryotes globally, possibly many times more if prokaryotes are included. Notable extinct animal species include non-avian dinosaurs, saber-toothed cats, and mammoths. Through evolution, species arise through the process of speciation. Species become extinct when they are no longer able to survive in changing conditions or against superior competition. The relationship between animals and their ecological niches has been firmly established. A typical species becomes extinct within 10 million years of its first appearance, although some species, called living fossils, survive with little to no morphological change for hundreds of millions of years, though this claim has been disputed.

Mass extinctions are relatively rare events; however, isolated extinctions of species and clades are quite common, and are a natural part of the evolutionary process. Only recently have extinctions begun to be recorded, and there is an ongoing mass extinction event caused by human activity. Most species that become extinct are never scientifically documented. Some scientists estimate that up to half of presently existing plant and animal species may become extinct by 2100. A 2018 report indicated that the phylogenetic diversity of 300 mammalian species erased during the human era since the Late Pleistocene would require 5 to 7 million years to recover.

According to the 2019 Global Assessment Report on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services by IPBES, the biomass of wild mammals has fallen by 82%, natural ecosystems have lost about half their area and a million species are at risk of extinction—all largely as a result of human actions. Twenty-five percent of plant and animal species are threatened with extinction. In a subsequent report, IPBES listed unsustainable fishing, hunting and logging as being some of the primary drivers of the global extinction crisis. In June 2019, one million species of plants and animals were at risk of extinction. At least 571 plant species have been lost since 1750. The main cause of the extinctions is the destruction of natural habitats by human activities, such as cutting down forests and converting land into fields for farming.
A dagger symbol (†) placed next to the name of a species or other taxon normally indicates its status as extinct.

sentence.text: A taxon may become functionally extinct before the death of its last member if it loses the capacity to reproduce and recover.
sentence.translation: 一个分类群如果失去了繁殖和恢复能力，可能在最后一个个体死亡之前就已功能性灭绝。
sentence.analysis: before 表示时间先后；if 引出条件；may 表可能。functionally extinct 与最后个体已死亡并非同一时间标准。

questions.prompt: 第一段区分功能性灭绝与最后个体死亡时强调什么？
options: 只要还有个体存活，就能保证种群持续繁殖和恢复
功能性灭绝只在最后一个个体死亡很久之后才发生
失去繁殖和恢复能力可能先于最后个体死亡
功能性灭绝表示物种只是暂时未被观察到，繁殖能力必定正常
